page: OVHcloud c2-60 is a compute-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. Memory capacity is 60.0 GB, yielding 3.75 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c2-60 in the average tier across most standard compute and memory tasks. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 1535.88, while multi-core performance reaches 24461.89. Memory bandwidth tests show 1775.09 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 120.4 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database and web serving operations, the instance achieves 25.27 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 16.25 GB/sec.

The older Intel Haswell architecture lacks modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and TSX, which impacts specialized workloads. This is evident in LLM inference benchmarks, where text generation speeds are weak, dropping to 49.64 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 6.54 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model, while prompt processing for a large 70B model is poor at 3.99 tokens/sec. Given these performance profiles and the dedicated physical cores, the server is suited for standard multi-threaded CPU tasks, static web serving, and basic database operations rather than modern AI inference.
